title: UPDATE: Mojo Delivers 41x Speedup Over Python in Initial Open Source Tests
summary:
Early performance benchmarks for the Mojo programming language show significant speed gains over Python for scientific computing, including a 41x increase in execution speed for specific data kernels. A user port of the iCorrVision software reduced the processing time of a uniaxial tensile test from 18.3 minutes using single-threaded Python to 26.7 seconds when utilizing 24 threads in Mojo. The same test run on a single Mojo thread finished in 3.3 minutes, representing a 5.6x improvement over Python.

Modular founder Chris Lattner also reported that the newly open MAX graph compiler has outperformed llama.cpp on mobile CPU and GPU hardware. These results follow the Oct. 23 announcement that the Mojo language and the MAX toolset, including its runtime internals and hardware abstraction logic, were made open for commercial development and extension.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Mojo and MAX are now fully open - for development, extension, and commercial use!
selectedTweets.text:
I'm happy to share that Mojo and MAX are now fully open - for development, extension, and commercial use! This includes the full Mojo programming language, but also the MAX graph compiler, MLRT runtime internals, and hardware abstraction logic.

Get your agents going!👇

Curiosity project: I ported the correlation kernel of iCorrVision, our open-source Python DIC software, to Mojo, and the speed-up is striking.

Uniaxial tensile test, every node, full test:
🐍 Python (1 thread): 18.3 min
🔥 Mojo (1 thread): 3.3 min (5.6x)
🔥 Mojo (24 threads): 26.7 s (41x)

Biaxial: 16.0 min → 32.0 s (30x).

Congrats @clattner_llvm on opening up Mojo and MAX! #Mojo #DIC #ExperimentalMechanics
